transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-24
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Iqbal (Redwood SE), Dmitri Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Tara Singh (Nimbus Head of Eng), Marco Ruiz (Procurement), Ellen Chu (Security), Priya Rao (Legal)

Summary (auto): quick triage of MSA exceptions, pricing band options, and KMS handoff notes. Some background noise, a few words mis-transcribed.

[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. My name's Jordan Park, account exec for Redwood Inference. We got Maya and Dmitri with me. How's everybody doing?
[00:12] Tara Singh: Good thanks. Sorry, bit of background noise—just wrapping a standup.
[00:18] Marco Ruiz: All good on our side. Marco in procurement.
[00:22] Ellen Chu: Ellen, security. We'll mostly jump in on the KMS and SOC2 bits.
[00:27] Priya Rao: Priya, legal. I'll be the contracts touchpoint.
[00:31] Maya Iqbal: Hi all — Maya SE, I'll cover the technical and the bench numbers you asked about.

[00:45] Jordan Park: Great. Quick agenda — triage the MSA exceptions Priya sent, run through pricing tiering options (hosted vs dedicated), KMS/HSM ownership questions with Ellen, and define next steps and who owns what. Sound right?
[00:58] Priya Rao: Yup that's what we need. We have a few non-starter items in the current MSA draft: data residency clause, audit rights window, and a confidentiality carve-out for our enterprise partners.
[01:12] Jordan Park: Understood. For the data residency — Redwood offers region pinning for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we can log region of inference and keep data controls, but we need to outline the egress and retention windows.
[01:30] Priya Rao: That's one of the ask — we need 90 day retention for logs and option to purge; also want commit to not use customer data to train models.
[01:42] Maya Iqbal: Technically, we don't feed production logs into model training. Our platform separates telemetry from model datasets, and we can toggle retention. I'll include exact retention config paths in the runbook I send.

[01:58] Ellen Chu: On KMS — we have two scenarios: we manage keys (Nimbus-managed KMS) or Redwood manages keys with customer-hold. We prefer customer-controlled keys in our cloud tenancy. Does Redwood support customer KMS/hardware-backed keys?
[02:17] Jordan Park: Yes, we support customer-supplied KMS in Private deployment and Dedicated with VPC-peered key management. For Hosted, we have an integration option where customers can bring keys via an HSM-backed flow but it's gated by commercial and engineering approval.
[02:33] Marco Ruiz: That's a gating factor for procurement — if we can't own keys, approvals will block. Pricing also depends on whether we go Dedicated — committed capacity — or Hosted pay-as-you-go.

[02:50] Maya Iqbal: To add to that, Dedicated gives predictable latency and throughput guarantees — the SLOs — and lower per-token pricing at commit bands. Hosted is faster to start but variable cost. There is also an intermediate: a private tenancy with reserved nodes.
[03:06] Tara Singh: Timeline-wise, we want a pilot in Q1 — two-week POC to validate latency for our interactive recommendation use-case, then a production rollout in Q2 if results are good.
[03:19] Jordan Park: Perfect, that's consistent with what we usually see. For the POC we can provision a Hosted test environment scoped to your traffic patterns and add a dedicated bench to show tail latency under simulated load. Maya will run that.

[03:35] Marco Ruiz: On pricing — we need a clear path to a committed band. Our CFO wants a threshold number to trigger a reserved capacity quote.
[03:44] Jordan Park: We'll send a pricing tiers spreadsheet that maps average monthly token usage to discount bands and Dedicated committed pricing. It will include the break-even points.
[03:53] Priya Rao: Back to MSA exceptions — we surfaced a clause around indemnity that we want tightened; also an exception for subcontractor audits. Does Redwood accept limited indemnity scope?
[04:07] Jordan Park: We typically push for a balanced indemnity. I'll send a redline-friendly version with our typical enterprise exceptions — that's what we do for larger customers. We'll flag the subcontractor audit path too.

[04:20] Ellen Chu: Couple technical security questions: do you provide tamper-proof audit logs, and can we get a retention export? Also for SOC2 — are you in scope right now and what's the carve-out?
[04:34] Dmitri Alvarez: Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified; we rotate reports annually and can provide a w/signing. For tamper-proof logs we offer write-once audit export and can configure retention and export endpoints to your S3. I'll share the report and the logging endpoints after this call.
[04:50] Tara Singh: Any egress fees? We run a lot of outbound traffic for our recommender enrichment.
[04:55] Jordan Park: There can be egress considerations depending on region and whether you use Dedicated or Hosted. We'll add egress fee scenarios to the pricing sheet.

[05:06] Marco Ruiz: Competitor question — LumenAI gave us a baseline with a cheaper per-token price but no KMS bring-your-own option. How do you stack there?
[05:16] Jordan Park: In a lot of cases we win on guarantees and predictable unit economics, plus the KMS/private deployment options. AtlasEndpoints may be similar, but Redwood's dedicated route includes SLA-backed latency. We'll put a short competitive note when we send the pricing.

[05:33] Priya Rao: On billing path, we prefer monthly invoiced commits versus pay-as-you-go CC billing. Is that supported?
[05:41] Jordan Park: Yes — we can do monthly invoiced reserved capacity for Dedicated with net-30 terms once procurement approves. For Hosted POC we usually go with CC/billing or a trial credit.

[05:54] Maya Iqbal: About the POC bench — quick technical note: our bench replicates warm cache and KV behavior; for interactive recommendations we need to test with a ~512 token context and sustained QPS to see tail latencies. I'll need sample traffic profile and a couple of prompt templates.
[06:14] Tara Singh: We'll share sample traffic and two prompt families by tomorrow end-of-day.

[06:21] Marco Ruiz: What about data residency — we need EU-only processing for specific customers. Can you guarantee region lock?
[06:30] Jordan Park: For Dedicated and Private yes; for Hosted we can route requests to an EU region and show proof, but contractual language will need to reflect how logs/backups are stored. We'll provide a data residency addendum option.

[06:44] Priya Rao: Also, we need to understand subprocessor lists and the ability to request removal or substitution for critical subprocessors.
[06:53] Dmitri Alvarez: We'll share our subprocessor list and the governance flow for removal requests; it's a standard part of our DPA.

[07:04] Ellen Chu: If we do customer-managed keys, who controls key rotation and revocation? If our keys get revoked does that cause downtime for inference?
[07:16] Maya Iqbal: In Private/Dedicated with customer-managed KMS, key rotation is controlled by the customer. We support rolling key rotations and have a fallback path where a short overlap is configured to avoid downtime. We'll document the exact rotation steps.

[07:31] Jordan Park: Ok — let's surface the net of these asks: Priya wants redline MSA with tightened indemnity and audit carve-outs; Ellen wants KMS architecture and rotation docs; Marco wants pricing tiers and egress scenarios; Maya will run bench tests for the POC.

[07:46] Priya Rao: Sounds right. One more governance note — our legal needs to see a 90-day log retention and a delete on request clause.
[07:55] Jordan Park: We'll incorporate that into the DPA options and call out purge APIs.

[08:02] Marco Ruiz: Who's the exec sponsor on Redwood side? Our CFO tends to like a named exec for big spend.
[08:09] Jordan Park: For commercial we can loop in our VP of Sales — I'll introduce them in the follow-up email when we hit the committed band step.

[08:18] Tara Singh: Timing: we'll try to lock approvals by early Feb. If Redwood can send the MSA redline and the pricing spreadsheet this week that helps procurement.

[08:27] Jordan Park: We will. Final question — any blockers we haven't surfaced?
[08:31] Ellen Chu: Just the KMS ownership and subprocessor removal timeline — if those are okay, security is comfortable.
[08:40] Priya Rao: Legal will review the redline and flag the indemnity specifics.

[08:46] Jordan Park: Great — recap of next steps: I'll send MSA redline + pricing tiers + competitive note; Maya sends bench plan and latency runbook; Dmitri will attach SOC2 and subprocessor list; Nimbus sends sample traffic and legal approver list. We'll aim for a follow-up early Feb and a POC in Q1.

[09:05] Marco Ruiz: Thanks all.
[09:07] Tara Singh: Thanks everybody.
[09:09] Jordan Park: Appreciate the time — we'll follow up with notes and the artifacts.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript fidelity: speaker boundaries occasionally overlapped and some product names were transcribed slightly off (eg Redwood "Dedicated" typed as "dedicated route" then "dedi-cated"), but overall medium quality copy.
